definition: A Naive Bayesian model is a classification technique based on Bayes' Theorem with an assumption of independence among predictors.
details: A Naive Bayesian model is a classification technique based on Bayes' Theorem with an assumption of independence among predictors. It is easy to build and particularly useful for very large datasets.

explainer.lead: A Naive Bayesian model is a classification technique built on Bayes' theorem that assumes independence among predictors. It is easy to build and particularly useful for very large datasets.

tiers.eli5: It sorts things into categories by scoring each clue on its own and combining the scores, which keeps it simple and quick even with lots of data.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers favour it when data is large and training speed matters; a pitfall is treating predictors as independent when in reality they influence each other, which can distort probabilities.
tiers.paperLevel: It classifies by selecting the class with the highest posterior, computed as the class prior times the product of per-predictor likelihoods under an independence assumption; probability estimates are often poorly calibrated.

explainer.example: For a customer dataset with many records, the model scores each class by multiplying prior and per-feature likelihoods and assigns the top-scoring class.
